title: BPC-157 vs TB-500
summary: Two sequences routinely catalogued together in tissue-model research, from entirely different structural origins — a 15-residue gastric-protein fragment against a 7-residue acetylated thymosin fragment.
narrative_html:
Why these two get shelved together

BPC-157 and TB-500 appear side by side in nearly every research catalogue, and the pairing is a matter of category rather than chemistry. Structurally they have almost nothing in common.

BPC-157 is a 15-residue peptide with free termini, derived from a partial sequence of a gastric protein, notable for a proline-rich core. TB-500 is a 7-residue N-acetylated fragment corresponding to residues 17-23 of thymosin beta-4. One is more than twice the length and 1.6 times the mass of the other, and their sequences share no motif.

The nomenclature trap

TB-500 is routinely described as "synthetic thymosin beta-4." The parent protein is 43 residues and roughly 4,960 g/mol; the fragment supplied under this name is 889 g/mol. A certificate quoting a mass near 4,960 for a product sold as TB-500 is describing a different molecule.

This is worth checking specifically when comparing suppliers, because vendor pages frequently quote the parent's residue count alongside the fragment's formula — an internal contradiction that indicates the description was not written from analytical data.

Handling differences

Both are water-soluble and neither carries cysteine, methionine or tryptophan, so both are chemically robust.

The practical divergence is charge. TB-500's two lysines against one glutamate give it net positive character, so it carries more counterion mass and adsorbs more readily to negatively charged plastic at dilute concentrations. BPC-157, with two aspartates and a glutamate against one lysine, is mildly acidic and less adsorptive.

TB-500's C-terminal glutamine is a slow deamidation site; BPC-157 has neither asparagine nor glutamine.

title: Semaglutide vs Tirzepatide vs Retatrutide
summary: Three acylated incretin analogues of increasing receptor breadth — single, dual and triple receptor activity — compared by residue count, mass and structural class.
narrative_html:
One design, three receptor breadths

These three represent successive generations of the same engineering programme, and the trend across them is receptor breadth rather than molecular size.

SemaglutideTirzepatideRetatrutide
Residues313939
Mass (g/mol)4,113.584,813.454,731.4
ReceptorsGLP-1GIP, GLP-1GIP, GLP-1, glucagon
LipidC18 diacidC20 diacidLipidated

Note that mass does not increase monotonically with receptor breadth: retatrutide engages three receptors and is lighter than tirzepatide, which engages two. Molecular size and functional complexity are not the same axis.

The shared architecture

All three use the same two-part stabilization strategy, and it is worth stating because it explains why they look alike analytically.

Aib substitution blocks dipeptidyl peptidase-4, the enzyme that inactivates native GLP-1 within minutes.

Lipidation through a linker provides reversible serum albumin binding, protecting the molecule from renal filtration and creating a circulating reservoir.

Neither modification alone suffices — one addresses enzymatic degradation, the other renal clearance — and the combination is the solved problem being reapplied across the family, with design effort going into receptor selectivity instead.

Why sequences are not published

A plain residue string would omit the Aib substitutions, the acylation site, the linker chemistry and the fatty acid — most of what distinguishes each molecule. Identity confirmation for all three rests on mass spectrometry against the complete modified structure.

Shared handling profile

All three are strongly hydrophobic for their length, retain late on reversed-phase columns, adsorb to plastic, and — unusually — aggregate more readily in concentrated solution than dilute, because the exposed lipid seeks a hydrophobic environment and often finds another molecule of the same compound. Reconstitute gently, aliquot immediately, and prepare working dilutions fresh.
